name: Alfalfa (lucerne)
benefits: High in protein for a green.
Rich in xanthophyll pigments that deepen yolk color.
cautions: High in fiber, so it dilutes the diet when fed in bulk. Offer the leafy parts as a treat.
Contains saponins, highest in midsummer growth. High levels are bitter and cut feed intake and growth.
Long stems in hay can cause crop impaction.

name: Amaranth
benefits: Leafy summer weed. Amaranth leaves have been tested as a broiler feed.
cautions: Do not feed raw amaranth seed as a grain. In feeding trials raw seed cut broiler growth, and in one Australian report chickens fed raw grain had convulsions and died. Birds nibbling seed heads on the plant is a different matter.
Pigweeds build up nitrates, most on heavily fertilized ground.
Contains oxalic acid. Fine as part of mixed forage, not as the only green every day.
